question.problem:
Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=4x-\frac{2}{x}$ at the point $(-1,-2).$

$x\,+$
{{field-1}}$\cdot \,y\,=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=4x-\frac{2}{x}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x-\frac{2}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x-2{x}^{-1}) \\  & =4+2{x}^{-2} \\  & =4+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(-1,-2):$

$$
m={f}^{′}(-1)=4+\frac{2}{(-1)^{2}}=4+2=6
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{6}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-2) & =-\frac{1}{6}[x-(-1)] \\ -6(y+2) & =x+1 \\ -6y-12 & =x+1 \\ x+6\cdot y & =-13.\end{aligned}
$$
